ruling.recommended_action: Close the dispute as no_action: the sole off-route segment is exempt under RD-4(a) and no refund is due; no account action (RD-6 conditions not met).
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a metered RydeTAXI ride, so extra kilometres enter the fare directly and RD-2's money is at stake [F6][RD-2]. The record contains exactly one off-route segment, 09:03–09:11, 3.97 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.80 km, +2.18 km, up to 1040 m off route [F3][RD-1]. Nothing on the rider's side exempts it: there is no in-app chat at all, so no rider message consented to any change before 09:03 [F7][RD-5], and the driver's post-trip statement that the rider agreed is a claim, not consent [F8][RD-5].

The exemption therefore turns on RD-4. The trace settles the RD-4(a) incident screen as ✓: the incident matched to this segment lies within 300 m of the replaced stretch of the optimal route (optimal km 2.1–3.9) and was reported before the detour [F12][F3][RD-4]. The system record is an accident reported 08:44 on Tampines Expressway (towards PIE) after Punggol Road Exit, 0 m from the optimal route, "avoid lane 1" [F12], i.e. a roadwork/accident-type event on the very road the optimal Punggol→Tampines route uses, in the trip window (pickup 08:56, drop-off 09:20) [F12][RD-4]. The supporting congestion record on that same optimal road is band 1 (0–9 km/h, severe) during 08:47–09:03 [F9][RD-4], which corroborates the blockage at the point that matters — the moment just before the driver left at 09:03 [F3][F9][RD-4]. On the record before me the segment is exempt: the driver proceeded by an alternative when the named optimal road was obstructed, which is the RD-4 reasonable cause, and no refundable segment remains.

The rider's timing objection (the detour ran 09:03–09:11, after the band-1 window closed at 09:03) [F3][F9] is a fair point but does not change the outcome: the corridor actually driven is corroborated as flowing (Punggol Road band 2, Tampines Avenue 12 band 4) [F10][F11], whereas the optimal road carried the accident and the worst band in the window [F12][F9][RD-4]; and RD-4(a) is established by the trace against the replaced stretch of the optimal route, which is the test the clause sets [F12][F3][RD-4]. RD-4(b) speed bands I use only as corroboration, not as an independent ground for exemption [F9][RD-4].

Billing is clean and confirms there is nothing to refund beyond the exemption: the total $29.26 is composed of published metered components — base $3.90, distance $17.48 for 12.40 km, time $6.41, platform $1.47, waiting $0.00, with no surge (1.0×) [F6][F5][FARE-1] — so FARE-1 yields no refundable item; this is not a fixed-fare service [F6][FARE-1]. The $3.61 excess-distance figure the rider seeks (2.56 km × $1.4097/km) [F4] is the metered kilometre charge for the exempt segment, which RD-4(a) places at no_action [F4][F3][RD-4][RD-2]. With the only segment exempt, the RD-2 sum is zero, which is consistent with the trace's allowed outcome.

No account flag: the driver has 0 route disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days over 1120 trips [F15], so RD-6's "repeated" condition (a prior upheld route dispute) is not met [F15][RD-6]. The rider's file (2 disputes, 0 upheld) is likewise clean [F14] and profile facts decide nothing on their own [F14][RD-6]. Safety screen: I read the complaint, the driver's statement and the (empty) chat — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears in any of them [F7][F8]; the rider's words are a billing protest ("I never agreed to any change") [F7], so safety_concern is "none". Evidence is sufficient: the record settles every element this ruling needs — a measured segment [F3], a matched, earlier-reported incident on the replaced stretch [F12], the corroborating speed band [F9], and the full metered fare breakdown [F6]; no gap affects the outcome.

segment_findings.reason: The sole off-route segment (09:03–09:11, +2.18 km) [F3] is exempt under RD-4(a): the trace matches an incident within 300 m of the replaced stretch of the optimal route (optimal km 2.1–3.9) reported before the detour — an accident at 08:44 on Tampines Expressway (towards PIE) after Punggol Road Exit, 0 m from the optimal route, 'avoid lane 1' [F12][RD-4] — with the same optimal road at speed band 1 (0–9 km/h, severe) 08:47–09:03 corroborating the blockage immediately before the driver left at 09:03 [F9][RD-4]. No rider message consented to any change (empty chat) [F7][RD-5], but RD-4 requires no rider agreement when the optimal route was obstructed by a recorded, earlier-reported incident [F12][RD-4].

rejected_claims.reason: The absence of any rider message (empty chat) [F7] means RD-5 consent is not established, but that does not make the segment unexempted: the segment is exempted by RD-4(a), whose conditions the trace settles as met by an earlier-reported incident on the replaced stretch of the optimal route [F12][F3][RD-4].

The driver's written statement alone [F8] is indeed not evidence, but RD-4(a) is satisfied by the system record itself — the accident reported 08:44 on the optimal road, 0 m from the route, matched within 300 m of the replaced stretch (optimal km 2.1–3.9) [F12][F3][RD-4] — which is a system record, not the driver's claim.

Flowing speed bands on the alternative corridor, Punggol Road band 2 and Tampines Avenue 12 band 4 [F10][F11], do not defeat the exemption: RD-4 turns on the obstruction of the replaced optimal stretch [F12][F9][RD-4], not on congestion of the diversion itself; those bands are at most corroboration and I do not rely on them [RD-4].

The requested amounts ($3.61 on 2.56 km, or ≈$3.07 on 2.18 km at $1.4097/km) [F4][F3] are computed only for unexempted segments under RD-2; here the single segment is exempt under RD-4(a) [F3][F12][RD-4], so the RD-2 sum is zero and no refund is payable.

Correct that no recorded rider consent exists (empty chat) [F7] and that the driver's statement is a claim, not consent [F8][RD-5]; but RD-4 provides an independent reasonable-cause exemption that requires no rider agreement [F12][F9][RD-4], so the absence of consent does not produce a refund.

Accepted as far as it goes: the total $29.26 is composed of published metered components with no surge and no waiting fee [F6][F5][FARE-1]; this supports no_action but is not itself a defence to the deviation — the deviation is excused by RD-4(a) [F3][F12][RD-4], not by the fare breakdown.
